value.title: Bounded history reads + crash-safe rotation (loadRecentHistory + archive)
value.description: Make agent-bober's append-only event log scale without breaking its existing programmatic consumers. Add a loadRecentHistory(projectRoot, { limit }) bounded tail reader and crash-safe rotation that moves the oldest entries to .bober/history.archive.jsonl once active history.jsonl exceeds a new history.maxActiveLines config field. loadHistory keeps its full-read contract by reading archive then active concatenated, so resume-cursor reconstruction and the EngineConformanceHarness observe an unchanged full stream. This is storage-layer only: no lessons store, no distillation, no CLI.

successCriteria.description: loadRecentHistory(projectRoot, { limit }) reads only active history.jsonl and returns at most `limit` entries newest-last; a unit test asserts the count cap and that no read is issued against history.archive.jsonl.

Rotation moves the oldest entries to .bober/history.archive.jsonl once active history.jsonl exceeds history.maxActiveLines, leaving at most maxActiveLines entries active; a unit test seeds maxActiveLines+50 entries and asserts active holds at most maxActiveLines and the archive holds the overflow.

loadHistory still returns every entry by reading archive then active concatenated; a unit test writes entries spanning a rotation and asserts loadHistory returns the full ordered set identical to the pre-rotation sequence.

Rotation neither drops nor duplicates entries when interrupted: a unit test simulating a crash between archive-append and active-truncate asserts the active+archive union contains every original entry exactly once.

history.maxActiveLines is a validated zod config field (positive integer, default 2000) in src/config/schema.ts; a schema test asserts the default applies on an empty config and a non-positive value is rejected.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0 and the existing src/state and conformance suites stay green with no new failures beyond the documented flaky tool-count baseline.

nonGoals: Do not change the exported signatures of loadHistory or appendHistory.
Do not alter resume-cursor or conformance logic beyond what regression tests need; their observable output must stay identical.
Do not migrate or rewrite the existing 272-line history.jsonl; rotation applies to new appends going forward.
Do not add any LLM, network, lessons-store, or CLI code — this sprint is the storage layer only.
stopConditions: Stop when loadRecentHistory, crash-safe rotation, and the maxActiveLines config exist, loadHistory still returns the full active+archive stream, and typecheck, build, and tests are green.
Stop when changes are confined to src/state/history.ts (and an optional src/state/history-rotation.ts), src/config/schema.ts, and their collocated tests.
value.definitionOfDone: History reads scale without breaking existing consumers: rotation keeps the active file bounded by history.maxActiveLines, loadRecentHistory offers a bounded tail read, and loadHistory still returns every entry by concatenating archive+active so resume-cursor and the conformance harness observe an unchanged full history. Rotation is crash-safe with no lost or duplicated entries, and typecheck, build, and the state/conformance tests pass.
assumptions: resume-cursor.ts already discards loadHistory's return value (resume-cursor.ts:19), so bounding reads cannot alter the reconstructed ResumeCursor.
conformance.ts deep-compares the full normalized history (conformance.ts:102,131), so loadHistory must keep returning the complete active+archive stream.
value.generatorNotes: Edit src/state/history.ts (or add src/state/history-rotation.ts and import it). Add archivePath(projectRoot) = .bober/history.archive.jsonl alongside historyPath. Implement rotation inside appendHistory (or a rotateIfNeeded helper called after append): count active lines; when > maxActiveLines, take the oldest (count - maxActiveLines) lines, append them to the archive file, then atomically rewrite active with the remaining tail using a temp-file + rename so an interruption never loses entries (append-to-archive first, then rename-new-active; on crash before rename, the worst case is duplicate-in-archive which the union test tolerates if you de-dup, OR keep archive-append idempotent by writing the new-active temp first then appending archive then renaming — pick one and document the ordering so C4 holds). Add loadRecentHistory(projectRoot, { limit }) that reads ONLY active history.jsonl, parses with the existing HistoryEntrySchema.safeParse, and returns the last `limit` entries. Update loadHistory to read archivePath (if present) then historyPath, concatenating archive-then-active, preserving existing skip-malformed-line behavior. Add `maxActiveLines: z.number().int().positive().default(2000)` to a history section in src/config/schema.ts (mirror PipelineSectionSchema style) and thread it to rotation (read from config, fall back to default 2000). Use import type for type-only imports; ESM .js specifiers; Unicode box-drawing section headers. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-1): bounded history reads + crash-safe rotation.
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify loadRecentHistory returns at most `limit` and does not touch the archive (spy on readFile path or assert via a temp project with a populated archive). Verify rotation leaves active <= maxActiveLines and the archive holds the overflow. Verify loadHistory over a rotated store equals the pre-rotation ordered sequence (write N entries, force rotation, assert loadHistory deep-equals the original ordered list ignoring nothing). Verify the crash-safety test: simulate interruption and assert the active+archive union has every entry exactly once. Verify the zod default (parse {} history -> maxActiveLines === 2000) and rejection of 0/-1. Run npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run build (exit 0), and the existing src/state + conformance tests; tolerate only the documented flaky tool-count baseline. Confirm git diff is confined to history.ts/history-rotation.ts, config schema, and collocated tests — no changes to resume-cursor.ts or conformance.ts logic.

value.title: Deterministic lessons memory store (LessonEntry schema + .bober/memory state module)
value.description: Add a new append-only lessons store under .bober/memory/, mirroring the MEMORY.md curated-index pattern. Introduce a zod LessonEntry schema whose sourceEntryRefs provenance array is mandatory and non-empty, persistence that writes one markdown file per lesson plus a single bounded INDEX.md line, and a capped index reader that never opens individual lesson files. This sprint is schema + persistence + bounded read only — no distillation logic, no CLI, no planner wiring.

successCriteria.description: LessonEntrySchema in src/state/memory.ts is a zod object with lessonId, createdAt, category, tags (string[]), summary, occurrences (positive int), severity (enum), and sourceEntryRefs (non-empty string[]); a test asserts a valid lesson parses and a lesson with an empty sourceEntryRefs array is rejected.

appendLesson writes .bober/memory/<lessonId>.md (front-matter plus body) and upserts a single one-line entry into .bober/memory/INDEX.md; a test asserts both files exist and INDEX.md gains exactly one line per distinct lessonId across repeated appends of the same id.

loadLessonIndex(projectRoot, { limit }) returns at most `limit` index records parsed from INDEX.md without opening any individual lesson file; a test asserts the cap and that no <lessonId>.md read is issued during the index load.

loadLesson(projectRoot, lessonId) round-trips a persisted LessonEntry, and the provenance invariant holds: every persisted lesson carries at least one sourceEntryRef; a test writes then reads a lesson and asserts equality plus a non-empty sourceEntryRefs.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0 and the new src/state/memory tests pass with no new failures beyond the documented flaky baseline.

nonGoals: Do not compute or distill lessons in this sprint — only the schema, persistence, and bounded index read.
Do not call any LLM, embedding, or network API.
Do not wire the planner or any CLI command to this store yet.
Do not read or modify history.jsonl in this sprint.
stopConditions: Stop when LessonEntry, appendLesson, loadLessonIndex, and loadLesson exist with passing round-trip and provenance tests and a bounded index read.
Stop when changes are confined to src/state/memory.ts and its collocated test.
value.definitionOfDone: A deterministic, append-only lessons store exists under .bober/memory/: each lesson persists as <lessonId>.md with structured front-matter and a one-line entry in a bounded INDEX.md, mirroring the MEMORY.md pattern. The zod LessonEntry schema enforces a non-empty sourceEntryRefs provenance array, loadLessonIndex offers a capped read that never opens individual lesson files, and typecheck, build, and tests pass.
assumptions: No .bober/memory directory exists today (verified via ls), so the store is greenfield and additive.
Mirroring src/state/history.ts (path helpers plus zod safeParse plus append) keeps the module consistent with existing state code.
value.generatorNotes: Create src/state/memory.ts mirroring history.ts conventions. Define memoryDir(projectRoot) = .bober/memory, lessonPath(root, id) = .bober/memory/<id>.md, indexPath(root) = .bober/memory/INDEX.md. LessonEntrySchema = z.object({ lessonId: z.string().min(1), createdAt: z.string().datetime(), category: z.string().min(1), tags: z.array(z.string()).default([]), summary: z.string().min(1), occurrences: z.number().int().positive(), severity: z.enum(['info','warn','high']), sourceEntryRefs: z.array(z.string().min(1)).min(1) }). appendLesson: ensureDir, write <id>.md as YAML-ish front-matter (between --- fences) carrying the structured fields plus a human-readable body, then upsert one INDEX.md line of the form `- <lessonId> [<category>/<severity>] (x<occurrences>) tags: a,b — <summary first 80 chars>`; upsert means replace the existing line for that lessonId or append if absent (read INDEX.md, split lines, filter out the prior line for this id, push the new line, rewrite). loadLessonIndex parses INDEX.md lines into lightweight records { lessonId, category, severity, occurrences, tags, summarySnippet } and returns the last `limit`. loadLesson reads <id>.md, parses the front-matter, and validates via LessonEntrySchema.safeParse. Use import type; ESM .js specifiers; box-drawing headers. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-2): deterministic lessons memory store.
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify LessonEntrySchema rejects empty sourceEntryRefs and accepts a valid lesson. Verify appendLesson creates <id>.md and a single INDEX.md line, and that appending the same lessonId twice keeps INDEX.md at one line for that id (upsert, not duplicate). Verify loadLessonIndex caps to `limit` and does not open per-lesson files (assert via spy or by deleting a <id>.md and confirming the index load still succeeds). Verify loadLesson round-trips a written lesson and the provenance invariant. Run npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run build (exit 0), and the memory tests. Confirm git diff is confined to src/state/memory.ts and its test.

value.title: Deterministic distillation + bober memory CLI (distill | list | show)
value.description: Add a pure, deterministic distill function that compresses sprint history plus eval outcomes into provenance-tagged LessonEntry records using only structured fields (recurring failed-criterion categories, repeated failing eval strategies, sprints exceeding an iteration threshold) — no LLM, no network call. Expose it through a new `bober memory distill | list | show` command. Distillation is idempotent: re-running adds no duplicate lessons. The command is the only entry point; nothing in pipeline.ts triggers it.

successCriteria.description: A pure distill(historyEntries, contracts) in src/orchestrator/memory/distill.ts returns a deterministic LessonEntry[] derived only from structured fields; a test over a fixed fixture asserts an exact expected lesson set, stable across repeated calls.

distill plus appendLesson is idempotent: running twice over identical input yields an INDEX.md with no duplicate lessonId, deduped by a content hash of category+tags+sourceEntryRefs; a test asserts the second run adds zero new index lines.
The distill path constructs no LLM provider client and performs no network call; a test asserts via a guard or spy that no provider is instantiated during distill().

`bober memory distill` reads full history via loadHistory plus contracts, writes lessons, and prints a count summary; `bober memory list` prints the bounded index; `bober memory show <lessonId>` prints one lesson with its sourceEntryRefs. A test invokes the handlers against a temp project and asserts the printed counts and that show renders provenance.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0 and the memory/distill and CLI tests pass with no new failures beyond the documented flaky baseline.

nonGoals: Do not use an LLM, embeddings, or any network call to produce or rank lessons.
Do not trigger distillation from pipeline.ts or any autopilot path — the CLI command is the only entry point.
Do not wire the planner to read lessons yet — that is sprint 4.
Do not change loadHistory or the LessonEntry schema from sprint 2.
stopConditions: Stop when distill is deterministic and idempotent, asserts zero LLM and network usage, and the three bober memory subcommands run against a temp project with passing tests.
Stop when changes are confined to src/orchestrator/memory/, src/cli/commands/memory.ts, the CLI command registration site, and collocated tests.
value.definitionOfDone: Running `bober memory distill` compresses sprint history into deterministic, provenance-tagged lessons with no LLM or network call, idempotently so a re-run adds no duplicates. `bober memory list` and `bober memory show` let a human inspect the store. The distill function is pure and unit-tested against a fixture, and typecheck, build, and tests pass.
assumptions: distill can read the full history via the existing loadHistory and the contracts via listContracts; sprint 1 hardening is not a prerequisite for correctness, only for scale.
A content hash over category+tags+sourceEntryRefs is a stable dedupe key for idempotency.
value.generatorNotes: Create src/orchestrator/memory/distill.ts exporting a pure `distill(history: HistoryEntry[], contracts: SprintContract[]): LessonEntry[]`. Derive lessons only from structured data: group eval failures by criterion category / verificationMethod, count recurrences, flag sprints whose iterationHistory length exceeds a threshold (e.g. >= evaluator.maxIterations). Each LessonEntry: deterministic lessonId from the content hash (no Date.now in the pure function — the CLI stamps createdAt when persisting, or pass a clock in), category, tags from the failure signature, summary from a fixed template, occurrences = count, severity by count band, sourceEntryRefs = the history entry identifiers / sprintIds the lesson aggregates. Keep distill side-effect-free; persistence happens in the command. Create src/cli/commands/memory.ts with subcommands distill|list|show mirroring sprint.ts structure; distill calls loadHistory + listContracts, runs distill(), persists via appendLesson (dedupe by hash), prints `distilled N lessons (M new)`. Register the command where other CLI commands register (mirror sprint registration). Add a test guard ensuring no provider import is exercised in distill(). Use import type; ESM .js specifiers. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-3): deterministic distillation + bober memory CLI.
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify distill() returns the same LessonEntry set across repeated calls on a fixed fixture and that lessons reference only structured fields. Verify idempotency: distill+persist twice, assert INDEX.md unchanged on the second run. Verify the no-LLM/no-network guard fires (assert no provider client constructed). Invoke the three subcommands against a temp project seeded with a history fixture: distill prints the count summary and writes lessons; list prints the bounded index; show <id> renders one lesson including sourceEntryRefs. Run npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run build (exit 0), and the new tests. Confirm git diff is confined to src/orchestrator/memory/, src/cli/commands/memory.ts, the registration site, and tests; confirm pipeline.ts has no new call into distill.

value.title: Planner reads bounded memory (close the arc) + demonstrably-improves gate
value.description: Close the feedback arc: wire the planner to retrieve a topK-bounded, deterministically-ranked set of lessons from the .bober/memory index at plan time, so it learns from past sprint outcomes without ever reading raw history.jsonl. Add retrieveRelevantLessons (tag/keyword overlap, index-only, hard-capped), update bober.plan Step 2 and agents/bober-planner.md to consume it, and document the close-the-arc flow plus its findPrecisionIssues A/B measure so the improvement is observable.

successCriteria.description: retrieveRelevantLessons(projectRoot, keywords, { topK }) returns at most topK lessons ranked by deterministic tag/keyword overlap, reading only INDEX.md; a test asserts the topK cap, that a matching keyword surfaces the expected lesson, and that a non-matching keyword returns an empty result.
The retrieval path reads .bober/memory/INDEX.md and never reads .bober/history.jsonl; a test asserts no read is issued against history.jsonl during retrieval.

Retrieved planner context is bounded: the serialized lessons block is capped at topK entries and a configured character budget; a test seeds more than topK lessons and asserts the serialized block respects both caps.

skills/bober.plan/SKILL.md Step 2 and agents/bober-planner.md instruct the planner to load the bounded lessons index via retrieveRelevantLessons (topK-capped) and explicitly forbid reading raw history.jsonl; a test or grep asserts both files reference the memory index and the topK cap.
npm run typecheck and npm run build exit 0 and the retrieval tests pass with no new failures beyond the documented flaky baseline.

A docs section documents the close-the-arc flow and the manual A/B measure (plan a feature with and without memory present, compare findPrecisionIssues counts), naming the metric and the expected direction; a reviewer confirms the documented procedure.

nonGoals: Do not feed lessons into the generator or evaluator — this sprint wires memory into the planner only.
Do not read history.jsonl from the planner or the retrieval path; only the bounded index may be read.
Do not introduce embeddings or semantic search; retrieval is deterministic tag/keyword overlap.
Do not auto-distill; the planner consumes whatever the explicit bober memory distill command last wrote.
stopConditions: Stop when retrieveRelevantLessons returns a topK-bounded, index-only result, the planner skill and agent are updated to consume it instead of raw history, the flow is documented, and typecheck, build, and tests are green.
Stop when changes are confined to src/orchestrator/memory/, skills/bober.plan/SKILL.md, agents/bober-planner.md, docs, and collocated tests.
value.definitionOfDone: The feedback arc closes: the planner retrieves a topK-bounded, deterministically-ranked set of lessons from the .bober/memory index at plan time and never touches raw history.jsonl. Retrieval and the serialized planner context are hard-capped, the bober.plan skill and bober-planner agent are updated to read the index, the close-the-arc flow plus its findPrecisionIssues A/B measure are documented, and typecheck, build, and tests pass.
assumptions: bober.plan Step 2 already reads project context files, so adding a bounded lessons-index read is a localized extension.
Deterministic tag/keyword retrieval over the bounded index is sufficient before the store outgrows the markdown pattern.
value.generatorNotes: Create src/orchestrator/memory/retrieve.ts exporting retrieveRelevantLessons(projectRoot, keywords: string[], { topK, charBudget }): it loads the bounded index via loadLessonIndex (sprint 2), scores each record by deterministic overlap between keywords and the record's tags/category/summarySnippet (e.g. count of shared lowercased tokens), sorts descending with a stable tiebreak (lessonId), and returns the top `topK`. Add a serializeLessonsForPlanner(records, { charBudget }) that renders a compact block and truncates to the character budget. Wire it: in skills/bober.plan/SKILL.md Step 2, add a bullet 'Read the bounded lessons index via retrieveRelevantLessons(keywords from the feature title/description, topK) — do NOT read .bober/history.jsonl directly'; in agents/bober-planner.md add the same instruction in the context-gathering phase. Add a docs section (docs/ or README) describing the close-the-arc flow and the findPrecisionIssues A/B measure. Keep retrieval pure and index-only. Use import type; ESM .js specifiers. Conventional commit: bober(sprint-4): planner reads bounded memory (close the arc).
value.evaluatorNotes: Verify retrieveRelevantLessons caps at topK, surfaces a lesson whose tags match a keyword, and returns empty for non-matching keywords. Verify it reads INDEX.md only and never history.jsonl (spy/path assertion). Verify the serialized block respects topK and the character budget when more than topK lessons exist. Grep skills/bober.plan/SKILL.md and agents/bober-planner.md for the retrieveRelevantLessons / memory-index instruction and the explicit prohibition on reading raw history. Confirm the docs section names findPrecisionIssues as the A/B metric and the expected direction (fewer precision issues with memory present). Run npm run typecheck (exit 0), npm run build (exit 0), and the retrieval tests. Confirm git diff is confined to src/orchestrator/memory/, the planner skill and agent, docs, and tests.
